events.title: Ellen Johnson Sirleaf becomes president of Liberia
events.summary: She is the first woman elected head of state of an African country.
events.description: On January 16, 2006, Ellen Johnson Sirleaf, the first woman elected head of state of an African country, was sworn in as president of Liberia.
events.notificationBody: In 2006, Ellen Johnson Sirleaf was sworn in as president of Liberia.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 16

events.title: El Salvador's civil war ends with the Chapultepec Peace Accords
events.summary: The government and the FMLN sign peace in Mexico City.
events.description: On January 16, 1992, the civil war in El Salvador ended as the government and the Farabundo Marti National Liberation Front signed the Chapultepec Peace Accords in Mexico City.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 16

events.title: NASA names its first women astronauts
events.summary: The new astronaut class includes six women.
events.description: On January 16, 1978, NASA announced its newest class of astronauts, which for the first time included six women.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 16

events.title: Charles V gives up the Spanish crown
events.summary: The emperor renounces his claim to Spain.
events.description: On January 16, 1556, Charles V, Holy Roman emperor and king of Spain, renounced his claim to Spain.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 16

events.title: The Pendleton Civil Service Act becomes law
events.summary: The US creates a merit-based Civil Service Commission.
events.description: On January 16, 1883, the Pendleton Civil Service Act established the Civil Service Commission in the United States.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 16

events.title: Popeye makes his debut
events.summary: The spinach-loving sailor first appears in the comic strip Thimble Theatre.
events.description: On January 17, 1929, Popeye, the sailor known for his love of spinach, made his debut in the comic strip Thimble Theatre.
events.notificationBody: In 1929, Popeye the Sailor first appeared in a comic strip.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 17

events.title: Benjamin Franklin is born
events.dateNote: New Style date; the Julian calendar then used in Britain's colonies gave January 6, 1705.
events.summary: The future scientist, writer and founding father is born in Boston.
events.description: On January 17, 1706, Benjamin Franklin was born. He later helped draft the US Declaration of Independence.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 17

events.title: Queen Liliuokalani of Hawaii is deposed
events.summary: A provisional government ends the Hawaiian monarchy.
events.description: On January 17, 1893, Hawaii's Queen Liliuokalani was deposed by a provisional government led by Sanford Ballard Dole.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 17

events.title: Eisenhower warns of the military-industrial complex
events.summary: The president's farewell address becomes famous for one phrase.
events.description: On January 17, 1961, in his farewell address, US President Dwight D. Eisenhower warned against the acquisition of unwarranted influence by the military-industrial complex.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 17

events.title: The Great Hanshin earthquake strikes Kobe
events.summary: A large earthquake hits the Osaka-Kobe region of Japan.
events.description: On January 17, 1995, a large-scale earthquake struck the Osaka-Kobe (Hanshin) metropolitan area of Japan, killing about 6,400 people.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 17

events.title: The German Empire is founded
events.summary: Otto von Bismarck's unification creates a new empire.
events.description: On January 18, 1871, the German Empire was founded under the leadership of Otto von Bismarck.
events.notificationBody: In 1871, the German Empire was founded.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 18

events.title: Eugene Ely lands a plane on a ship
events.summary: The first aircraft landing on a ship's flight deck.
events.description: On January 18, 1911, the American pilot Eugene Ely performed the first aircraft landing on a ship's flight deck.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 18

events.title: Sierra Leone's civil war is declared over
events.summary: A decade of conflict officially ends.
events.description: On January 18, 2002, the civil war in Sierra Leone was officially declared over. More than 50,000 people are estimated to have died.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 18

events.title: Willie O'Ree breaks the NHL's color barrier
events.summary: He is the first Black player in a National Hockey League game.
events.description: On January 18, 1958, Willie O'Ree became the first Black athlete to play in a National Hockey League game.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 18

events.title: A.A. Milne is born in London
events.summary: The creator of Winnie-the-Pooh is born.
events.description: On January 18, 1882, A.A. Milne, the author who created Winnie-the-Pooh, was born in London.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 18

events.title: Verdi's Il trovatore premieres in Rome
events.summary: The opera is first performed.
events.description: On January 19, 1853, Giuseppe Verdi's opera Il trovatore premiered in Rome.
events.notificationBody: In 1853, Verdi's opera Il trovatore premiered in Rome.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 19

events.title: Edgar Allan Poe is born in Boston
events.summary: The master of the macabre is born.
events.description: On January 19, 1809, the writer Edgar Allan Poe was born in Boston.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 19

events.title: A US patent is granted for storing food in tin cans
events.summary: Ezra Daggett and Thomas Kensett patent a preserving process.
events.description: On January 19, 1825, Ezra Daggett and Thomas Kensett obtained a patent for a preservation process used to store food in tin cans.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 19

events.title: Eisenhower holds the first televised presidential press conference
events.summary: Cameras are allowed into a presidential news conference.
events.description: On January 19, 1955, US President Dwight D. Eisenhower held the first-ever televised presidential press conference.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 19

events.title: Barack Obama is sworn in as president
events.summary: He becomes the first African American president of the United States.
events.description: On January 20, 2009, Barack Obama was sworn in as the 44th president of the United States, the first African American to hold the office.
events.notificationBody: In 2009, Barack Obama was sworn in as the 44th US president.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 20

events.title: The Iran hostage crisis ends
events.summary: Fifty-two Americans are released after 15 months.
events.description: On January 20, 1981, the Iran hostage crisis ended when 52 Americans who had been held hostage for 15 months were released.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 20

events.title: James Cook lands on Kauai
events.summary: The British explorer comes ashore at Waimea in Hawaii.
events.description: On January 20, 1778, the British explorer James Cook landed at Waimea, on the island of Kauai in Hawaii.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 20

events.title: Amilcar Cabral is assassinated
events.summary: The leader of Guinea-Bissau's independence struggle is killed.
events.description: On January 20, 1973, Amilcar Lopes Cabral was assassinated while leading the effort to secure Guinea-Bissau's independence.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 20

events.title: Federico Fellini is born
events.summary: The celebrated Italian film director is born.
events.description: On January 20, 1920, the Italian director Federico Fellini, one of the most celebrated filmmakers of the post-World War II period, was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 20

events.title: Concorde begins commercial service
events.summary: The supersonic airliner starts carrying passengers.
events.description: On January 21, 1976, Concorde, a supersonic commercial aircraft built with funding from the British and French governments, began regular service.
events.notificationBody: In 1976, the supersonic Concorde began commercial flights.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 21

events.title: Louis XVI is executed in Paris
events.summary: The last Bourbon king of France before the Revolution is guillotined.
events.description: On January 21, 1793, during the French Revolution, Louis XVI, the last Bourbon king of France before the Revolution, was executed by guillotine in Paris.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 21

events.title: Vladimir Lenin dies
events.summary: The founder of the Soviet state dies.
events.description: On January 21, 1924, Vladimir Lenin, the founder of the Soviet state, died.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 21

events.title: Christian Dior is born
events.summary: The fashion designer is born in Granville, France.
events.description: On January 21, 1905, the fashion designer Christian Dior was born in Granville, France.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 21

events.title: Placido Domingo is born in Madrid
events.summary: The operatic tenor is born.
events.description: On January 21, 1941, the singer Placido Domingo was born in Madrid.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 21

events.title: Queen Victoria dies
events.summary: Britain's queen dies after a reign of more than 60 years.
events.description: On January 22, 1901, Queen Victoria died at age 81 after reigning for more than 60 years.
events.notificationTitle: The end of the Victorian age
events.notificationBody: In 1901, Queen Victoria died after more than 60 years on the throne.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 22

events.title: Bloody Sunday in St. Petersburg
events.dateNote: January 9 in the Julian calendar then used in Russia.
events.summary: Troops fire on marching workers, sparking revolution.
events.description: On January 22, 1905, Russian workers marching in St. Petersburg were fired on by Russian troops. The day became known as Bloody Sunday.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 22

events.title: Evo Morales becomes president of Bolivia
events.summary: He is Bolivia's first president of Indigenous descent.
events.description: On January 22, 2006, Evo Morales was sworn in as president of Bolivia, the first person of Indigenous descent to hold that office.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 22

events.title: Roberta Bondar becomes Canada's first woman in space
events.summary: The neurologist flies aboard the space shuttle.
events.description: On January 22, 1992, Roberta Bondar became the first Canadian woman and the first neurologist to travel into space.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 22

events.title: Lord Byron is born
events.summary: The Romantic poet is born.
events.description: On January 22, 1788, Lord Byron, the British Romantic poet and satirist who captured the imagination of Europe, was born.

sources.name: Encyclopaedia Britannica - On This Day: January 22
